# Errors

The stable taxonomy of spec §43. Codes never change meaning, so a script may match on them; the `name` is the selector `try`/`catch` and predicates over error values use.

| code | selector | kind | meaning | what to do |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Ono-Sendai-E0001` | `parse.syntax` | parse | The input is not valid Ono syntax. | Read the span the diagnostic points at; the construct there cannot become valid however much more you type. `help language` lists the syntax of every statement form. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0002` | `parse.incomplete` | parse | The input ended in the middle of a construct; more text would complete it. | Close the open string, bracket or block. Interactively the editor keeps the line open; in a script the file ended early. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0101` | `resolve.command_not_found` | resolution | No keyword, function, native command or executable answers to this name. | Check the suggestions the error carries, or run `help` to browse commands. `explain <name>` reports every resolution step that was tried (ADR-0011). |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0102` | `resolve.target_not_found` | resolution | The verb is known but has no such target. | Run `help <verb>` to list the targets that verb accepts, or `get command` to browse the registry. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0103` | `resolve.ambiguous` | resolution | The name matches more than one candidate and no namespace was given. | Qualify the name with the namespace of the candidate you meant, for example `ono:get` or `dev.example.tool:scan`. The error lists every candidate's qualified name. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0201` | `type.mismatch` | type | A value did not have the type the operation requires. | `type <expression>` shows what the value actually is. Convert it explicitly rather than relying on coercion. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0202` | `type.unknown_field` | type | A record schema has no such field. | `type` on the stream shows the schema and its fields. A field that exists but is unknown to the provider is `null`, not a missing field (spec §10.5). |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0203` | `type.invalid_unit` | type | A unit was unknown, or two incompatible dimensions were compared. | Compare like with like: byte sizes with byte sizes, durations with durations. The unit suffix must be adjacent to the number, as in `512MiB`, not `512 MiB`. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0301` | `io.not_found` | io | The path or resource does not exist. | Check the path; `get file <parent>` lists what is actually there. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0302` | `io.permission_denied` | permission | The operating system refused access to the resource. | The current user lacks the required permission. Elevate explicitly rather than re-running blind; `explain` reports the privilege a command needs before it runs. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0303` | `io.already_exists` | io | The resource already exists and would have been overwritten. | Choose another destination, or pass the command's explicit overwrite option. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0304` | `io.not_directory` | io | A path component is not a directory. | One of the leading components of the path is a file; check the path spelling. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0401` | `provider.unavailable` | provider | The provider cannot answer on this system right now. | The backing system is absent or not running — no systemd on this host, no container runtime socket. `get command <name>` names the provider a command needs. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0402` | `provider.unsupported` | provider | The provider does not implement this capability. | Another provider for the same target may support it. The capability matrix generated from `docs/contracts/capabilities.yaml` lists which provider answers what. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0403` | `provider.schema_violation` | provider | A provider emitted a value outside the schema it advertises. | This is a defect in the provider, not in your pipeline. Report it with the output of `inspect` on the offending value. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0404` | `provider.inconclusive` | provider | The answer is empty or incomplete, and that establishes nothing about the system. | The provider looked and did not find, and it is telling you that not finding is not the same as absence here — a retention window that may have discarded what you asked about, a search that could not reach every scope, a verification that ran out of time. The message says what was and was not established. Treat an empty pipeline downstream of this as unknown, never as "nothing happened". |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0405` | `provider.authentication_failed` | permission | The external system did not accept the credential the provider presented. | The credential is absent, expired, revoked or malformed — the remote system said *who are you*, not *you may not*. Renew it where it came from: a credential helper's login flow, a rotated token, a client certificate that is still valid. Nothing was performed, and this is never the same as `provider.authorization_denied`, which is a refusal to a known identity. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0406` | `provider.authorization_denied` | permission | The external system refused the operation to the identity the provider presented. | The identity was accepted and the operation was refused to it — `403` and its relatives. The operation was not performed. This is data about what you may do, never evidence that the target is absent (external-system-provider §18.1); a read refused here is a coverage gap, and a write refused here changed nothing. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0407` | `provider.rate_limited` | timeout | The external system asked the provider to slow down. | A `429` or its equivalent, with the retry guidance the system gave in the error metadata where it gave any. A bounded, idempotent read may already have been retried once within its budget before this was reported; a mutation is never replayed on your behalf (external-system-provider §20.2, §20.3). Narrow the query or wait. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0501` | `external.exit_nonzero` | external | An external process exited with a non-zero status. | The status is carried in the error metadata. Use `||` to branch on it, or `try`/`catch` to handle it as a value. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0502` | `external.signal` | external | An external process was terminated by a signal. | The signal name is carried in the error metadata. A signalled process did not choose its exit status, so treat it differently from a non-zero exit. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0601` | `remote.unreachable` | provider | The remote link could not be established or was lost. | `test host <name>` probes reachability and reports where the attempt failed. An established link that dropped mid-pipeline reports the values it had already delivered. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0602` | `remote.protocol_mismatch` | provider | The remote peer speaks an incompatible protocol version. | Upgrade the agent on the remote host, or connect in agentless mode where the local side does the work. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0603` | `remote.host_key_changed` | safety | The remote host presented a different key than the one recorded for it. | Do not override this because it is inconvenient. Verify the new key out of band, then record it deliberately. A changed key is indistinguishable from an interception. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0604` | `remote.identity_permissions` | safety | The peer identity file is readable or writable by someone other than its owner. | The file holds the private key that is this machine's identity on a direct link (v0.4.1 section 8.3). `chmod 600` the path named in the diagnostic. A key another account could read is a key another account can impersonate you with, so this is a refusal and not a warning; nothing is printed from inside the file. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0605` | `remote.peer_unauthenticated` | safety | The remote peer did not prove possession of a peer key. | A direct link is mutually authenticated in v0.4.1 (section 7.1, section 13.3) and never retries without a certificate. A peer that speaks the older, one-sided direct protocol is refused here; upgrade it, or reach it over `--transport ssh`, where OpenSSH authenticates the host instead. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0701` | `safety.confirmation_required` | safety | The operation needs explicit confirmation that this context cannot ask for. | Scripts and non-interactive sessions never wait for a TTY (spec §17.4). Re-run interactively, or pass the command's explicit confirmation option. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0702` | `safety.policy_denied` | safety | A configured safety policy forbids the operation. | `get config safety.*` shows the policy and the layer that set it. Config mode denies external execution, network access and plugin load by design (ADR-0010). |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0801` | `stream.unbounded_operation` | stream | The operation requires bounded input but the stream is unbounded. | `sort`, `group`, `count` and `measure` need a finite input. Bound the stream first with `take <n>` or a window. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0802` | `stream.cancelled` | cancelled | The stream was cancelled before it completed. | Cancellation propagates through native pipelines and becomes a signal for external processes (spec §18.5). Values already delivered remain valid. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0803` | `stream.backpressure_timeout` | timeout | A consumer did not accept values within the configured budget. | The slow stage is named in the error metadata. Raise the budget, or insert a bounded stage such as `take` ahead of the consumer. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0901` | `adapter.not_available` | resolution | No adapter answers to this invocation, and structured output was required. | Only an explicit structured demand raises this (`adapt …`, or a pipeline whose consumer needs objects). Drop the demand to run the program raw, or decode its output yourself with `from json`; `explain` names the adapters that were considered. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0902` | `adapter.disabled` | permission | An adapter exists for this invocation but is switched off in this context. | The error metadata names the adapter and the setting that disabled it. The raw program is still one `raw` away. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0903` | `adapter.unsupported_invocation` | provider | The adapter knows the executable but not this combination of options. | `help adapter <id>` lists the invocations the adapter supports. Where the pipeline did not require structure the program already ran raw; the metadata says whether it did. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0904` | `adapter.version_incompatible` | provider | The executable's version is outside the range the adapter was tested with. | The metadata carries the version found and the range supported. A machine-format adapter may still work — `adapt` forces it — but a version-constrained parser refuses by design (spec v0.3 §1.46). |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0905` | `adapter.executable_mismatch` | resolution | The executable that resolved is not the one the adapter's contract names. | A program earlier on PATH shadows the one the adapter was written for; `explain` shows the path that resolved. The program ran raw, or will if you drop the structured demand. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0906` | `adapter.rewrite_failed` | provider | The adapter could not turn the invocation into its machine-oriented form. | This is an adapter defect; the metadata names the adapter and its version so it can be reported. `raw <command>` runs the program as typed. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0907` | `adapter.decode_failed` | provider | The executable's output was not what the adapter's decoder expects. | The raw bytes are kept in the error metadata and nothing was fabricated. Check the executable's version against the adapter's range, and run the program `raw` to see its output as it is. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0908` | `adapter.schema_violation` | provider | The adapter decoded a value outside the schema it advertises. | The offending field and the schema are in the metadata. This is an adapter defect; report it with the executable version, and use the raw program meanwhile. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0909` | `adapter.capability_denied` | permission | The adapter's package is not allowed to run this executable. | `process.exec` grants a package exactly the executables its manifest declares (spec v0.3 §1.22). `get plugin` shows the grant; the raw program is unaffected. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0910` | `adapter.conflict` | conflict | More than one adapter claims the invocation and the resolution rules cannot separate them. | The metadata lists the candidates. Prefer one in the adapter configuration, or disable the other; until then the program runs raw. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E0911` | `adapter.required_for_structured_pipeline` | type | A consumer demanded objects and no adapter can provide them for this invocation. | A stage declared over objects is never handed the bytes a program wrote, and a forced structured invocation never downgrades to text (spec §12.3, spec v0.3 §1.18). Run the program raw, decode the output yourself (`| from json`), or drop the structured consumer. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1001` | `spatial.not_found` | resolution | No place, object or alias answers to this spatial selector. | `look` lists the exits of where you stand and `near` lists what is adjacent to it; both answer without a name being known in advance (spec v0.4 §9). `find place <text>` searches the index across domains. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1002` | `spatial.ambiguous_selector` | resolution | More than one place answers to this selector and none of them is the obvious one. | The error metadata lists the candidates. Narrow the selector — `follow socket :443` rather than `follow socket` — or use `near <relation>` to stand where all of them are visible. A script never gets a picker: ambiguity is deterministic and fails (spec v0.4 §29.3). |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1003` | `spatial.not_enterable` | type | This object exists but is not a place you can stand in. | `enter` moves into a place; the registry's `enterable` flag says which object types are one (spec v0.4 §41.1). Read the object with `get`/`inspect` instead, or enter the collection that contains it. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1004` | `spatial.no_relation` | resolution | No relation of that name leaves this place. | `look` names the exits this place has, and `docs/contracts/spatial/relations.yaml` is the whole vocabulary (spec v0.4 §41.2). A relation that exists but has no neighbour here answers `spatial.not_found` instead — the name was understood. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1005` | `spatial.no_parent` | resolution | This place has no canonical parent, so `up` has nowhere to go. | `up` follows the canonical hierarchy and the root is its top (spec v0.4 §6.6, §11.1). Use `back` to retrace the trail you actually took, or `home` to return to the root. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1006` | `spatial.history_empty` | conflict | The navigation trail holds no earlier place to return to. | `back` retraces the trail of this session, which starts empty and is not persisted across sessions (spec v0.4 §46.1). `trail` shows what it holds; `up` moves by hierarchy instead of by history. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1007` | `spatial.destination_gone` | resolution | The place the trail or pin points at no longer exists. | The metadata carries the tombstone — when the object went away, and the replacement candidate where one can be identified (spec v0.4 §10.3, §20.3). The trail record is kept; `back` again skips to the nearest place that still exists. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1008` | `spatial.permission_denied` | permission | This user may not see the objects or relations behind this place. | Denied is not empty: the group stays visible with its state so the boundary is legible (spec v0.4 §35.2). Spatial navigation never escalates privilege on its own; run the inspection deliberately as a user who may read it. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1009` | `spatial.unsupported` | provider | No installed provider can answer for this place, relation or domain. | An unavailable domain stays visible and says why rather than disappearing (spec v0.4 §4). `get provider` lists what this build can answer; a KUANG/11 package may contribute the missing objects. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1010` | `spatial.stale` | provider | The index's answer is older than this operation is allowed to accept. | The index is a cache and providers remain the truth (spec v0.4 §33.2). The metadata says when the object was last observed; re-run the command to revalidate, and note that a mutation always revalidates its target before it acts. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1011` | `spatial.remote_unavailable` | provider | The remote host this place belongs to cannot be reached. | A remote root is an explicit space and crossing to it is never implicit (spec v0.4 §19, §35.4). `get link` shows the links this session holds; `link host <name>` establishes one deliberately. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1012` | `spatial.scope_violation` | permission | The movement would cross a scope boundary this session may not cross. | Host, container, namespace and mount boundaries are visible on purpose (spec v0.4 §2.18, §35.4). `trail` shows the boundary that was refused; enter the scope explicitly instead of reaching through it. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1013` | `spatial.map_too_large` | stream | The requested map exceeds its node budget and cannot be drawn honestly. | A map clusters rather than truncates arbitrarily (spec v0.4 §8.2), and refuses when even clustering would not fit. Narrow the scope, lower the zoom level, or raise `spatial.map.node_budget`. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1014` | `spatial.identity_conflict` | conflict | Two observations claim to be the same object and their identities disagree. | Reconciliation refuses rather than merging two objects into one place (spec v0.4 §37.1, §42.1). The metadata names both identities and the providers that asserted them; this is a provider defect worth reporting. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1401` | `spatial.cost_refused` | resource | The planner estimated this query beyond the interactive budget and refused it. | v0.4.1 §33.3: a query the planner predicts beyond the supported interactive budget is refused or answered at a bounded lower detail, rather than left to look hung. The message names the estimate and the number of candidates it was made over (§34.1), so the refusal can be acted on. Narrow the place, lower the depth, or ask for the expensive relation explicitly — §34.3 requires that path to exist. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1101` | `resource.item_limit` | resource | An operation reached the number of values it is allowed to retain. | The metadata names the stage that enforced the ceiling, the configured limit and the consumption that crossed it — never the retained values, because a resource error that prints its payload is a second resource problem (v0.4.1 §21.4, §53.3). Narrow the input, or raise `limits.materialize_items` deliberately. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1102` | `resource.byte_limit` | resource | An operation reached the number of bytes it is allowed to retain. | Bytes are counted with the deterministic approximate estimator of §21.2, so the figure is a logical payload size rather than resident memory. Narrow the input, or raise `limits.materialize_bytes` deliberately. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1103` | `resource.materialization_limit` | resource | An operation that must see its whole input may not materialize this input. | The refusal is about the input as a whole rather than about a count that was reached: the stage requires finite input, or its budget admits nothing at all (v0.4.1 §22.2, §22.3). Bound the upstream before the stage that needs it whole. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1201` | `remote.unauthenticated` | safety | The connecting client proved possession of no key, so there is no identity to authorize. | A direct link is mutually authenticated (v0.4.1 section 7.1). The listening agent has no mode that accepts a client without a certificate, and authorization cannot begin without an authenticated identity (section 2.2). Connect with an `ono` that presents a peer identity. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1202` | `remote.unauthorized` | safety | The client is authenticated but is not listed in the agent's authorization store. | Holding a private key proves who you are, never that the operator wants you here (v0.4.1 section 9.1). On the agent's host, `add client-key <fingerprint>` authorizes the client to observe; the diagnostic carries the fingerprint to add and whether a store exists at all. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1203` | `remote.capability_denied` | safety | The client is authorized, but not for the capability this request needs. | Grants name exact capability ids and never patterns (v0.4.1 section 9.5). The metadata says whether observe access is off or the action capability is absent; `set client-key <fingerprint> --allow <capability>` on the agent's host grants exactly the one named. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1204` | `remote.authorization_store_invalid` | safety | The authorization store could not be loaded, so nothing is authorized. | A malformed store is never read as an empty one and never falls back to permissive access (v0.4.1 section 9.2, section 59.5). The diagnostic names the file and the line; repair that line, or remove the file to authorize nobody deliberately. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1501` | `remote.connection_limit` | resource | The listening agent is already holding as many connections as it may. | A listening agent has a hard ceiling on concurrent connections and a second one per authenticated client key (v0.4.1 section 12.1, section 12.3). The metadata names which of the two was reached and the figure it was set to. The refusal is retryable: a slot is released whenever a session ends. `limits.remote_connections` and `limits.remote_connections_per_client` configure the two ceilings on the agent's host. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1502` | `remote.handshake_timeout` | timeout | The peer did not complete TLS and Ono negotiation within the time a handshake is given. | A peer that opens a connection and then says nothing holds a slot in the agent's pre-negotiation ceiling for free, so the handshake has a deadline (v0.4.1 section 12.2). Ten seconds by default, configured on the agent's host with `limits.remote_handshake_timeout_ms`. A link dropped this way is worth retrying: nothing about the client was refused. |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1601` | `plugin.not_found` | resolution | No installed package and no catalog entry answers to the plugin reference. | `find plugin <word>` searches the installed set and every catalog; `get plugin` lists what is installed. A short name is the package's `name`, a canonical id its reverse-DNS `id`, and `./dir` or `path:<dir>` an explicit local package (K11P section 4.1). |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1602` | `plugin.reference_ambiguous` | resolution | The short name resolves to more than one canonical package. | The metadata lists every candidate as a canonical id and a `<catalog>/<name>` selector. Name one of those; nothing is chosen by catalog order or by publisher (K11P section 10.3). |
| `Ono-Sendai-E1603` | `plugin.catalog_unavailable` | resolution | The catalog names the release and its artifact is not available to this build. | This build fetches nothing over the network. | `Ono-Sendai-E1606` | `plugin.transport_refused` | safety | A plugin artifact would travel over a transport policy does not allow. | A catalog artifact is fetched over HTTPS. | `Ono-Sendai-E1301` | `temporal.invalid_time` | parse | Time selector cannot resolve unambiguously. | A selector is an instant (`2026-08-31T12:17:00+02:00`), a local date and time, a time today, a relative past duration (`-10m`) or an event (`event @e42`) — v0.5 §4.4.
